ai.title: Add verify checks to Layer 2 sponsored skill schema
ai.summary: The Layer 2 sponsored skill schema in `common/src/ads/sponsored-skill-layer2.ts` now accepts an optional `verify` array, limited to `LAYER2_MAX_VERIFY` items, where each entry defines a case-insensitive regex check against source files. ai.title: Add thinking level presets for single-model catalogs
ai.summary: The model picker preset logic in `common/src/util/freebuff-model-presets.ts` now detects when a catalog lists exactly one model with a reasoning ladder and returns that model's thinking levels instead of the standard tier-based stops. A new `thinkingLevelPresets` helper maps the lowest, default, and highest rungs to the efficient, balanced, and powerful slots using labels like "Fast", "Default", and "Max". The `FreebuffModelPreset` interface gains a `thinkingLevel` flag to identify these single-model ladders, and `matchingFreebuffModelPreset` treats a manual effort override as custom rather than hiding it behind a category label.

entries.title: CLI update: sponsored-agent

ai.title: Add install tool to CLI sponsored runs
ai.summary: Sponsored CLI runs can now add packages through the new install tool, which replaces the previous shell-install guidance and bypasses the shell-install refusal when active. The tool validates the package name and version, detects the project's package manager from its lockfiles, and calls the server's resolver before executing the canonical command with scripts disabled. The shared install-decision logic in `common/src/ads/sponsored-declared-installs.ts` now returns the tool-specific refusal text `SPONSORED_LOCAL_INSTALL_TOOL_REFUSAL` when the tool is registered for the run.
ai.evidence: The diff adds the `install_package` tool registration in `cli/src/utils/sponsored-run.ts` and `cli/src/utils/sponsored-agent.ts`, introduces `SPONSORED_INSTALL_TOOL_NAME` in `common/src/ads/sponsored-install-tool.ts`, and swaps the shell-install prompt bullet for `SPONSORED_INSTALL_TOOL_GUIDANCE_BULLET` when the tool is active.

changes.what: Registers the install tool for CLI sponsored runs and adds the tool-specific prompt guidance that replaces the shell-install bullet.
Adds the shared install tool handler, input schema, project-detection helper, and the package resolver wire shape used by all surfaces.
Updates the sponsored install command evaluator to return the tool-specific refusal when the tool is active and exports the canonical install helper and manager constants for the tool to reuse.

eli5.text: When an advertiser funds a coding task that runs on your computer, the assistant now adds a new way to install software packages that is safer and more automated than before. Instead of the assistant typing install commands into your terminal, it now uses a built-in tool that checks with the server whether a package is allowed, picks the correct version, and installs it without running any hidden scripts that could harm your project. This change only affects people who accept and run these advertiser-sponsored tasks in their terminal; it does not change how you use the free AI coding assistant for your own projects, and you do not need to update your settings or take any action.

ai.title: Add run summary scrubber and version 3 onboarding conversions
ai.summary: This commit adds a dedicated module for advertiser-facing run summaries that scrubs sensitive data and bumps the sponsored conversion tools capability to version 2. The new simpleConversionDefinitionSchema restricts version 3 conversions to onboarding-only evidence (sign-in, API key, or product download) without model-authored goals or instructions, and the merged agent evidence schema now distinguishes browser observations from host installation verification. The run summary instruction is injected into sponsored run prompts and step driver reports, while the evidence parser validates and scrubs the agent's closing explanation against the 800-character limit before it crosses the wire. Five other files update bench documentation, client support gates for the new conversion version, and Layer 2 skill compilation to support optional conversion definitions and package-free native HTTP integrations.

entries.title: CLI update: freebuff-chat-controls

ai.title: Freebuff chat admission opens model picker on refusal or running turn
ai.summary: The Freebuff CLI chat admission flow now opens the model picker instead of retrying when a refusal leaves the user with no valid model, or when a message is queued behind an active turn. A new `chooseModel` flag on the `ChatAdmission` type marks refusals that require a model switch, and the `enterAction` helper in the chat controls component maps these states to a picker-opening Enter action. The `freebuffTurnRunning` utility extracts the running-turn check, which gates the admission hook so that a queued message can change its model before sending.
ai.evidence: cli/src/state/freebuff-chat-store.ts adds a `chooseModel` boolean to the `ChatAdmission` type and `admissionInFlight` helper; cli/src/components/freebuff-chat-controls.tsx introduces the `enterAction` function which opens the model picker when `admission.chooseModel` is true or when `waitingOnTurn` is active; cli/src/hooks/use-freebuff-chat-admission.ts extracts `freebuffTurnRunning` to consolidate stream and chain progress checks.
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the specific user journey that triggered the addition of the `waitingOnTurn` gate, only that it prevents admission during an active chain.

eli5.text: When Freebuff blocks a message because you lack enough time for the chosen model or because a previous task is still running, the assistant now opens the model selection menu instead of just showing an error. This lets you switch to a different AI model immediately without canceling your draft or starting over. You notice this when pressing Enter on a blocked message now presents a list of available models to choose from, rather than requiring you to manually go back to the start screen or use a command to change settings.
